problem_statement: sharetribe/dev-docs is the Sharetribe Developer Documentation site, built with Nextra 4 on Next.js 15 and exported as a static site under the /docs base path. Its documentation shell hosts an on-page section navigator, the DocsSectionNav ('On this page'), rendered at the top of the content area of every documentation route. The navigator shows the current page's section jump chips with the active section highlighted, plus a release-channel switcher whose live readout names the docs channel the reader is on ('Reading: Stable release channel'). The current build has four regressions: (1) the navigator is mounted only on the landing page, so every other docs route loses its 'On this page' navigator; (2) the chip and channel rows are pinned to a fixed 720px track that never wraps, so on a 390px phone the rows spill past the viewport and the whole documentation page scrolls sideways; (3) the navigator is restyled to an off-brand dark-slate slab that clashes with the light Sharetribe docs shell; and (4) clicking a release-channel chip visibly highlights it but the readout never updates, staying 'Stable' even after 'Edge' is selected. Restore the DocsSectionNav so it renders on every captured documentation route, its chip and channel rows reflow and fit within a 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow, it uses the on-brand Sharetribe orange-accent styling within the light/dark docs shell with a legible active chip, and the channel readout updates to name the channel the reader has selected. Desktop and tablet layout of the surrounding Nextra docs chrome (navbar, collapsible sidebar, footer, article, search) must remain intact on every route.
required_content: The DocsSectionNav 'On this page' navigator must render at the top of the content area on every captured documentation route (the landing page and the /introduction page), not just the landing page.

The navigator's section jump-chip row and release-channel row must wrap or otherwise reflow so that on a 390px mobile viewport the document has no horizontal overflow beyond a small tolerance; desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) must remain overflow-free.

The navigator must adopt the on-brand Sharetribe docs visual language (light/dark shell, orange accent) with a legible active section chip -- not an off-brand dark slab and not an illegible pale-on-pale active chip.
Selecting a release-channel chip (Stable / Edge / Legacy) must update the live readout to name the selected channel (e.g. 'Reading: Edge release channel') while the chosen chip is marked active.
The Nextra docs shell around the navigator -- navbar, collapsible sidebar, footer, article content and search -- must remain intact and reachable on every captured route.
design_constraints: Preserve the Sharetribe Nextra docs visual language: the light/dark theme, Circular typography, the orange accent, and the navbar/sidebar/footer chrome.

The section jump chips and channel switcher must remain a horizontal strip on desktop and tablet; on mobile the rows should wrap onto multiple lines rather than clipping, hiding, or masking overflow with a document-level overflow-x:hidden clip.
The active section chip and the active channel chip must stay legible against their background (no pale-on-pale or dark-on-dark contrast failures).
The release-channel readout must reflect the reader's live selection on every render; do not snapshot a label once at mount.
Keep the navigator scoped to the docs content area; do not alter the Nextra theme files, the page content, or the surrounding chrome.
state_constraints: desktop_home captures the docs landing page at 1440px, where the DocsSectionNav sits as a single horizontal 'On this page' navigator (section jump chips + channel switcher) above the docs content with no horizontal overflow and the active chip legible on the orange accent.

mobile_home captures the docs landing page at 390px; in the baseline the navigator's fixed 720px rows spill the document past the viewport, and the repaired site must reduce that overflow to within tolerance while keeping all chips present and legible.
tablet_home captures the docs landing page at 834px, confirming the navigator rows stay overflow-free at tablet width.
desktop_intro captures the /introduction docs page at 1440px, confirming the navigator renders on a second route (cross-page presence) and the docs article/sidebar/footer remain intact.
mobile_intro captures /introduction at 390px, confirming the cross-page navigator and the overflow repair hold on a second route.
channel_toggle_home captures the landing page at 1440px after clicking the 'Edge' release-channel chip; the readout must update to name the Edge channel while the Edge chip is marked active.

change_completion: The DocsSectionNav renders on every captured route (landing + introduction), restoring the cross-page 'On this page' navigator.
Clicking the Edge channel chip updates the readout to name the Edge release channel.
All section jump chips and channel chips remain present and legible after the repair on both mobile and desktop.
design_consistency: The navigator adopts the on-brand Sharetribe orange accent within the light/dark Nextra docs shell, with a legible active chip.
Desktop and tablet keep the horizontal navigator; only the mobile layout reflows onto multiple rows.
The surrounding Sharetribe docs navbar, sidebar, footer, and typography are preserved.
regression: The static docs export still serves every captured route without console or network errors.
The navbar, sidebar, footer, article content, and search remain reachable and unchanged.
responsive: 390px home and introduction pages have no horizontal overflow beyond tolerance after the repair.
Desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts remain overflow-free and visually unchanged.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Repair/state_continuity task on the Sharetribe Nextra docs site. The lever is the site's native on-page section navigator (an 'On this page' TOC plus a release-channel switcher), a genuine docs-framework feature mounted from app/layout.jsx and rendered on every documentation route. The reference navigator renders cross-page, reflows on mobile, uses the on-brand orange accent with a legible active chip, and its channel readout tracks the live selection. Four orthogonal discriminators separate the legs: cross-page presence (dom_assertions), mobile overflow (no_horizontal_overflow), on-brand legible styling (visual_regression over the navigator crop), and the channel readout wiring (interaction_assertions). The original-defect baseline fails presence, overflow and visual fidelity but wires the channel readout correctly (passes interaction); the smart-wrong non-fix additionally snapshots the readout at mount so the Edge click leaves it stale. Console and network are clean on all legs across all captured routes.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Sharetribe Developer Documentation, a Nextra 4 + Next.js 15 static-export docs site with a rich navbar/sidebar/footer shell. Its on-page section navigator (an 'On this page' TOC with a release-channel switcher) is a native docs feature that hosts four orthogonal regressions -- cross-page presence, mobile overflow, off-brand/illegible styling, and a stale channel readout -- giving a deterministic L4 state_continuity repair with visual and interaction discriminators.
